newsitem.title: UK: Bentalls sees firm outlook, eying buyouts.
newsitem.headline: Bentalls sees firm outlook, eying buyouts.

text.p: British retail group Bentalls Plc is eyeing suitable acquisitions to expand its chain as it continues to improve its financial position in its current financial year.

Bentalls, which has its flagship superstore in Kingston, south of London, reported on Wednesday a 12.4 percent increase in sales to 97.3 million stg for the 53 weeks to February 1, 1997. Its pre-tax profit rose to 3.7 million stg from 1.2 million in the previous year.
Group chief executive Grenville Peacock said it was now keen to expand by acquring single units, out side the southeast, possibly in in the Midlands.
"There are opportunities and we are looking at them," Peacock told Reuters. He, however, said chances of an acquisition this year was slim.
He was optimistic on Bentalls' current year's performance saying it had maintained a 11 percent like-for-like sales growth till last week.

He said the group was expecting to shrug off any consumer uncertainty caused by the election because spending should be boosted by the cash payouts by several building societies which are floating on the stock market.

A portion of the group's improved cash position is being used to refurbish its 130,000 square foot department store in Bristol, due to open in Autumn 1998. Bentalls is spending 26 million stg on the project.
"The improved financial strength of the company gives us a firm base from which we can progress and we can look forward to a substantial addition to the group's trading assets...," the company said.
